drafts.title: Provide longer front-seat thigh support and at-least-competitive rear legroom for tall occupants
drafts.description: Tall drivers must experience longer front-seat cushion support and rear passengers must have legroom no worse than main competitors in the segment so tall occupants are comfortable on long trips.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat cushion effective thigh-support length increases by at least 60 mm versus the current model when measured from the seatback reference point; rear legroom (knee point to seatback) must meet or exceed the median value of the top 3 segment competitors in each market as measured in a standardized benchmark test.
assumptions: Benchmark uses the OEM-standardized measurement for 'knee point to seatback' and a consistent driver position for all vehicles.
Top 3 competitors per market can be identified and measured at launch.
A 60 mm extension of effective thigh support is feasible within packaging targets for the successor model.
uncertainties: Exact packaging and crash-structure constraints may limit achievable cushion extension in some markets.
Competitor dimensional data availability and measurement variability between labs.

drafts.title: Cup holders that accept common bottles and large tumblers without tipping or excessive rattle
drafts.description: Customers must be able to place common water bottles and 1 L tumblers in the cup holders and drive without items tipping or rattling excessively.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders must securely accommodate cylindrical containers with diameters between 50 mm and 90 mm and retain a 1 L tumbler during 0.3 g lateral acceleration without tipping or producing audible rattles above 45 dB in 95% of trials.
assumptions: Typical market bottles and tumblers fall within the 50–90 mm diameter range; the 1 L tumbler represents an upper bound.
Test method for lateral acceleration and audible rattle follows an internal OEM protocol.
uncertainties: Extremely wide or non-cylindrical containers may still require adapters.
Acoustic thresholds for 'excessive' rattle vary by user; 45 dB chosen as engineering-acceptable limit.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate opens reliably on the first gesture in real-world use
drafts.description: When customers use the hands-free gesture to open the tailgate it should work reliably on the first attempt across typical footwear, gait and loading conditions so they do not have to repeat the gesture.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The hands-free tailgate opens to the programmed setpoint within 3 seconds on the first valid gesture in >=95% of test trials across a defined set of footwear types and with typical rear bumper loads; a failure is defined as no opening or requiring a repeat gesture within 5 seconds.
assumptions: Tests include representative footwear types (e.g., boots, sneakers) and common cargo loads behind the bumper.
Environmental obstructions that block the gesture area are excluded from the success metric.
uncertainties: Performance may vary with aftermarket bumper attachments, heavy mud/snow, or obstructive clothing.
Sensor-field interference in very crowded parking environments could reduce first-attempt success.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with substantially more colors and fine brightness control saved per user
drafts.description: Customers must be able to choose from a broad palette of ambient colors and set brightness in finer steps, with the chosen illumination saved to their driver profile.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Provide at least 64 distinct user-selectable colors and at least 10 discrete brightness levels (including a near-off night mode); the selected color and brightness are stored and recalled per driver profile.
assumptions: Vehicle electrical and lighting architecture supports the increased palette and brightness control.
Driver profiles already exist and can be extended to store lighting preferences.
uncertainties: Exact perceptual spacing of 64 colors may vary by material and cabin surface reflections.
Regulatory limits on interior lighting brightness in some markets could constrain maximum levels.

drafts.title: Seat memory that reliably restores saved positions across cycles
drafts.description: When a customer recalls a saved seat memory the seat must return to the same driving position reliably, including after ignition cycles and battery disconnects.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Selecting a saved memory restores the seat position within ±20 mm linear tolerance and ±2° angular tolerance of the stored settings in >=95% of activations, including after ignition off/on and after a 30-minute battery disconnect test.
assumptions: Stored memory includes seat track, backrest angle, steering column and mirror presets as currently supported.
Measurement uses the OEM seat-position metrology method.
uncertainties: Extreme low/high temperature conditions or mechanical wear over time could affect repeatability.
Calibration drift after long service intervals may require maintenance actions.

drafts.title: Flush door handles that operate reliably in freezing temperatures
drafts.description: Customers must be able to open the vehicle using the flush door handles in freezing weather without the handles freezing shut or requiring manual de-icing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Flush door handles must unlock and open on the first user action in at least 19 of 20 trials at ambient temperatures down to -20°C, with standard road salt exposure and after a 4-hour static exposure period.
assumptions: Tests use standard salt spray and freeze-thaw cycles representative of winter road conditions in target markets.
Users perform the normal unlock action (keyfob or touch) prior to an opening attempt.
uncertainties: Extreme icing conditions beyond test protocol (e.g., thick ice sheets) may still prevent operation.
Aftermarket protective films or covers could alter freezing behavior.

drafts.title: 12 V trunk power outlet for running portable coolers
drafts.description: Customers must be able to plug a portable cooler into a dedicated 12 V socket in the trunk so they can run cooling devices during travel or when parked.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Provide a trunk-located 12 V socket rated to supply up to 120 W and positioned so a typical portable cooler plug can be used without clearing major cargo; outlet must be available in accessory mode so it can power coolers when the vehicle is parked.
assumptions: 120 W covers the majority of common portable coolers customers intend to use.
Outlet placement will follow typical trunk-use ergonomics so cords do not route across sharp edges.
uncertainties: Some high-draw coolers may exceed 120 W and require dedicated external power.
Regulatory or electrical architecture constraints in certain markets could limit continuous power availability while parked.

drafts.title: Front-end meets new EU pedestrian protection regulation (request for compliance)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the vehicle front end meets the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope in this requirements set: regulatory homologation and specific design solutions will be handled during certification and engineering validation.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/homologation requirement requested by customers (EU pedestrian protection). Certification and specific compliance measures are out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbag FMVSS 208 certification request (customer asks for certification)
drafts.description: Customers request that the rear-seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope in this requirements set: specific certification activities and filing are handled by homologation teams; this draft records the customer request.
drafts.scope_reason: Certification/homologation request (FMVSS 208); legal and certification work is out of scope for product feature drafts.

drafts.title: Headlights follow ECE R112 beam pattern rules in markets that require it (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the headlights follow ECE R112 beam pattern rules in every market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope in this requirements set: regulatory compliance and homologation per-market are handled by engineering/homologation; this draft records the customer request.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/homologation request (ECE R112); compliance work is out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for a specific 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder for the volume knob (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers specifically requested that the volume knob use a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: specific component/part-level engineering specifications are recorded but not included as customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification for a specific component (encoder). Customer-facing requirement would state the user outcome (e.g., 'adjust volume without looking'); component choice is out of scope.

drafts.title: Request for 4.5 mm laminated side windows (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the side windows use 4.5 mm thick laminated glass.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: specific material thickness is an engineering specification and will be evaluated by engineering and NVH/safety teams.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/material specification (glass thickness) requested by customers; component-level choices are out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³ (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the seat cushion uses foam with a density of 55 kg per cubic meter.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: specific foam density is an engineering/material specification to be assessed by seat engineers and NVH/comfort teams.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/material specification (foam density); exact material choices are out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Customer request for BMW-guaranteed residual value after five years
drafts.description: Customers ask that BMW guarantees a residual value of 60% after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: pricing, guaranteed residuals, and financial commitments are business/financial decisions and not part of product feature requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Business/financial request (residual value guarantee); pricing and guarantees are out of scope.

drafts.title: Customer request to reduce production cost per car by 8%
drafts.description: Customers asked that BMW cuts the production cost per car by 8 percent.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: production cost targets are internal/manufacturing objectives and not customer-facing product requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Manufacturing/cost target request; production cost reductions are out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
